newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African parliament plans hearings on EU trade.
newsitem.headline: S.African parliament plans hearings on EU trade.

text.p: South Africa's parliament plans to hold public hearings in Cape Town on Monday on the government's trade negotiations with the European Union.
The South African government is preparing a negotiating mandate in response to tough instructions given by the European Council earlier this year to its negotiators.
Members of parliament resolved a month ago to insist on a role in preparing South Africa's negotiating position even though this was not their constitutional right.

Nedlac, the statutory National Economic Development and Labour Council, grouping unions, business and government, will discuss the South African mandate for the next round of talks with the EU in Johannesburg on Thursday.

Janet Love, African National Congress chairwoman of the parliamentary committee on agriculture told Reuters her group and the committees on trade and industry and foreign affairs would follow up with joint public hearings on Monday.
Unions, business and members of the public who had given prior notice would then be free to make submissions to the committee, she said.
Love said the committee would not seek to dictate specific aspects of the negotiating mandate, but would make a report to the government on the mandate process and principles.

The EU has denied South Africa full accession to the Lome Convention on trade with developing countries in Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific on the grounds its economy is too sophisticated. Instead, the EU has adopted a mandate to negotiate a free trade area agreement that excludes up to 40 percent of South African agricultural products. At the same time, the EU calls on South Africa and its neighbours rapidly to lower tariff barriers against European imports.
Officials have said South Africa's mandate could be ready for cabinet consideration this month, but they say an agreement with the EU might not be concluded before 1998.
